> Some of these Wformat-truncation are a pain to fix. Tempted to disable them, I'm not up for fixing all of them.

For now, at least.  The *right* fix would be to use a "generate a string and make it big enough to hold the full string" routine, but that involves doing some level of memory management even if it's just picking the right scope (and possibly making sure we don't overwrite string pointers, although maybe just letting the scope destroyer clean up discarded strings suffices), so, yeah, it's not a simple fix.

(libpcap and tcpdump are also dealing with -Wformat-truncation.)

commits_data.title: CMake: Disable Wformat-truncation (GCC warning)
commits_data.message:
CMake: Disable Wformat-truncation (GCC warning)

Converting from GLib functions to stdio.h turns up many of these
warnings. They are disabled to allow work to go on and until
there is consensus on how to handle them.

    -Wformat-truncation
    -Wformat-truncation=1

        Level 1 of -Wformat-truncation enabled by -Wformat employs
        a conservative approach that warns only about calls to bounded
        functions whose return value is unused and that will most likely
        result in output truncation.
